footnotes.text: WhileD&C 84:23–27tells us that the Melchizedek Priesthood was withdrawn from Israel in Moses’ day, the Prophet Joseph Smith taught that prophets of Israel held it (seeTeachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith,compiled by Joseph Fielding Smith [1976], 180–81). It follows that prophets also knew the gospel, though they were restricted in what they could teach the people (seeAlma 12:9).

For a summary of the sources and structure of the Book of Mormon, see Eldin Ricks,Story of the Formation of the Book of Mormon Plates(1966), 1–7; see also S. Kent Brown,From Jerusalem to Zarahemla: Literary and Historical Studies of the Book of Mormon(1998), 28–54.
The following prophets were roughly contemporary with Lehi: Huldah (see2 Kgs. 22:14–20), Jeremiah, Obadiah, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah.
This prophecy is typical of the writings of the other prophets in Lehi’s generation. Compare Huldah in2 Kgs. 22:15–17; Jeremiah inJer. 5:1–10; Habakkuk inHab. 1:1–10; and Zephaniah inZeph. 1:1–18.

For comments on Zenos’s contributions, see Bruce R. McConkie, “The Doctrinal Restoration,” inThe Joseph Smith Translation: The Restoration of Plain and Precious Things,edited by Monte S. Nyman and Robert L. Millet (1985), 17–18; Bruce R. McConkie,A New Witness for the Articles of Faith(1985), 558–59, 563.
The Book of Mormon was first offered for public sale on 26 March 1830, and the Church was organized 11 days later, on 6 April.
